Context: this page continues the table begun on the previous page, headed 'I. Zur Ausschließung gewisser Zahlen beim Aufsuchen der Factoren' ('On the exclusion of certain numbers when searching for factors'). The Latin title reads: 'Forms that contain all numbers m some multiple of which, when the given number D is added to it or subtracted from it, gives a square.' In modern terms: for each signed D, list the reduced residue classes of m, modulo the conductor of Q(sqrt D), with Kronecker symbol (D/m) = +1. For a prime m this is exactly the condition that D is a quadratic residue mod m. The modulus is |D| if D ≡ 1 (mod 4) and 4|D| otherwise. If D > 0 the character is even, so classes come in pairs ±r and Gauss writes '±' with representatives r < modulus/2. If D < 0 the character is odd and he writes '+' with all representatives. These are the linear forms of divisors of x^2 - D (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae arts. 147-150), used in the exclusion method of factoring (DA arts. 329-334).

Upper block (prime D, modulus |D|, all D ≡ 1 mod 4). By reciprocity (D/m) = (m/|D|), so each list is the set of quadratic residues mod |D|. For D ≡ 1 mod 8 the residues are folded to ±r with r ≤ (|D|-1)/2. My recomputation:
- +53: 13 reps 1,4,6,7,9,10,11,13,15,16,17,24,25. Correct; the blotted entry between 17 and 24 was a slip removed by Gauss.
- -59: 29 residues 1,3,4,5,7,9,12,15,16,17,19,20,21,22,25,26,27,28,29,35,36,41,45,46,48,49,51,53,57. Correct, including the inserted 25.
- +61: 15 reps 1,3,4,5,9,12,13,14,15,16,19,20,22,25,27. Correct.
- -67: 33 residues. Correct.

- +97: 24 reps 1,2,3,4,6,8,9,11,12,16,18,22,24,25,27,31,32,33,35,36,43,44,47,48. Correct; 47 is written over another digit.

The vertical bars and semicolons in the rows look like counting/segmenting aids (the residue range cut into roughly eighths). They have no arithmetic content.

- -34 (136k): 32 classes. The first 20 lie below 68. The remaining 12 are 136 - m for m < 68 with χ(m) = -1 (odd character). Correct.

errors: +31 (124k ±): 53 is listed but should not be. Jacobi (31/53) = (53/31) = (22/31) = (2/31)(11/31) = 1·(-1) = -1; directly, 31 is not a square mod 53. The row has 16 representatives where φ(124)/4 = 15 are expected.

-29: the image shows a corrected digit in '81,?3'. The correct class is 93 (93 = 3·31, χ = 1·1), not 83 (χ(83) = (-1/83)(83/29) = -1·(25/29) = -1). If the digit is read as 83 it is an error; read as 93 it is correct.
+89: the first (struck-out) line contained wrong entries such as 12/13, 19 and 38. Gauss himself cancelled it and rewrote it correctly.
Blotted entries in +53, +73, +33, -33 and +34 are self-corrected slips; the remaining lists are correct.

results.what: Tables of quadratic residues for primes 53-97 (folded to ± representatives when p ≡ 1 mod 4), giving the linear forms of divisors of x^2 - D
results.modern_name: Quadratic residues / linear forms of prime divisors of x^2 - D via quadratic reciprocity
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Legendre (Essai sur la théorie des nombres 1798, tables of linear divisors), Gauss (Disquisitiones 1801, arts. 147-150)

results.what: Residue classes mod 4|D| (or |D|) with Kronecker symbol (D/m) = 1 for composite or even D (±30, ±31, ±33, ±34, ±35, -29, -37), exploiting the parity of the character to give ± representatives or complementary classes
results.modern_name: Kernel of the Kronecker character (D/·) of conductor |disc Q(√D)|; genus/class tables for the exclusion method of factorization

deep.surprise_reason: These are computational auxiliary tables (linear forms of divisors of x^2 - D) of exactly the kind described in the Disquisitiones and used for Gauss's exclusion method of factoring. They are routine and well known as his, apart from one small error (53 in the +31 row).
